facts.statement: In life, Elektorornis was slightly smaller than a sparrow.
facts.quote: In life, it would have been slightly smaller than a sparrow

facts.statement: Alexander D. Clark and Jingmai O'Connor (2021) concluded that Elektorornis likely had a toothless beak to pry into wood, using its elongated toe to acquire prey.
facts.quote: Alexander D. Clark and Jingmai O'Connor (2021) observed that extant animals with similar probing structures consistently have additional anatomical traits that allow the animal to penetrate a hard substrate, such as wood. The researchers concluded that Elektorornis likely would have had an edentulous (toothless) beak to pry or gouge into wood, allowing it to use its uniquely elongated toe to acquire prey.

facts.statement: Elektorornis belongs to the parent group Enantiornithes.
Elektorornis is classified in the class Reptilia.
Elektorornis lived during the Cenomanian stage, between 100.5 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)
